correctness.rationale: For every real h>0, the ten supporting facets consist of two square caps and eight triangular side faces, giving sixteen edges; sign-flips of adjacent facet normals characterize contour edges of the orthographic shadow. In the dihedral fundamental wedge z>0,x>=y>=0, the sign indicators A=(x+y<sqrt(2)gz), B=(x-y<sqrt(2)gz), C=(x<gz), D=(y<gz), g=(1-1/sqrt(2))/(2h), produce N=6+A+C-|B-D|. The four radial thresholds order C<A<B<D for azimuth <pi/8 and A<C<D<B after pi/8. The radial CDF F(r)=1-1/sqrt(1+r^2), integrated in azimuth using J_g(t)=asin(sin(t)/sqrt(1+g^2)), yields P(5)=8(2J(3pi/8)-J(pi/4)-J(pi/2))/pi, P(7)=8(2J(pi/8)-J(pi/4))/pi, P(8)=1-8J(pi/8)/pi, P(6)=the complement. Each radial interval exists on a positive-measure azimuth wedge, so all four probabilities are positive for EVERY finite h>0. I separately computed planar monotone-chain shadows for 800 deterministic random directions each at h=.1, h=2^(-3/4), h=3: every hull count agreed with the derived sign-count identity. The original verification script also reconstructs facets/horizons and estimates integrals, but its historical 72,000-hull claim was read in source, not rerun in this audit. Finite calculations supplement, not prove, the continuous quantified law.

value.rationale: A complete, exact Haar viewing distribution for a simple natural one-parameter family of antiprisms identifies four strictly positive shadow types at every height and a height-independent angular chamber transition pi/8. This quantitative visibility invariant distinguishes geometry that the mean silhouette formula cannot. The four explicit arcsine masses are independently reusable benchmarks for stochastic geometry, exact shadow computation, and polar section counts; the result is not merely a code check or a small arbitrary instance.
residual_risks: Restricted to the canonical pi/4 twist and equal circumradii; wider deformations and joint area/perimeter distributions remain open.
